title: Walk without your phone
easy: Walk around the block. Leave the phone at home.
medium: Walk for twenty minutes with no phone and no destination.
brave: Walk for an hour with no phone. Find your way back by memory.
indoor: Leave the phone in another room and walk slowly through your home for ten minutes.
why: Attention you don't hand away is attention you keep.
pen: Write sentences that begin with "Right now I notice..." for two minutes.

title: Ask someone a real question
easy: Ask someone how their day actually went, and listen to the whole answer.
medium: Ask someone what they are looking forward to this month. Ask one follow-up.
brave: Ask someone you know only a little what matters most to them right now.
indoor: Call someone and ask one question you have never asked them before.
why: Most people are rarely asked. Listening is a gift you can give today.
pen: Write what they said. Then write what you assumed before they said it. Keep the two apart.

title: Keep the first hour
easy: No phone for the first fifteen minutes after you wake up.
medium: No phone for the first hour after you wake up.
brave: No phone until you have finished one real piece of work.
indoor: Put the phone in a drawer before breakfast and take it out only after.
why: Whoever gets your first hour shapes the rest of the day. Let it be you.
pen: Write three sentences that start with "I have to". Rewrite each as "I choose to" or "I won't".

title: Name five sounds
easy: Stop for one minute and name five sounds you can hear.
medium: Sit outside for five minutes. Count the different sounds without judging them.
brave: Spend fifteen minutes somewhere busy, only listening. No music, no phone.
indoor: Close your eyes by an open window for three minutes and listen.
why: Observation comes before interpretation. Practice the first part.
pen: Make two columns: what I heard, and what I thought about it.

title: Choose a small discomfort
easy: End your shower with ten seconds of cold water.
medium: End your shower with one full minute of cold water.
brave: Take a fully cold shower, slowly, breathing through it.
indoor: Hold a plank until it becomes uncomfortable. Then hold it for five more breaths.
why: Practicing small discomfort makes larger discomfort less frightening.
pen: Make two columns: what was up to me today, and what was not.

title: Make something by hand
easy: Draw the object nearest to you. Five minutes, no erasing.
medium: Cook one meal from scratch without a video.
brave: Build or repair something you have been putting off.
indoor: Fold, sketch or write something with your hands for fifteen minutes.
why: Making things returns you to the present. Your hands don't scroll.
pen: Write what went well today, what didn't, and what you will do differently tomorrow.

title: Look up
easy: Go outside and look at the sky for two full minutes.
medium: Find a place with a wide view and stay there for fifteen minutes.
brave: Watch the sunrise or the sunset from start to finish.
indoor: Stand at a window and watch the clouds or the light change for five minutes.
why: The sky is large and your worries are small. Both are true.
pen: Describe today as if you were watching it from very high above. Keep it short.

title: Thank someone specifically
easy: Thank someone for one specific thing they did, in person.
medium: Tell someone one thing they do that makes your life better, and why.
brave: Thank someone you have never properly thanked: a teacher, a neighbour, an old friend.
indoor: Call someone and tell them one specific thing you are grateful for.
why: Gratitude said out loud is different from gratitude you only feel.
pen: Write an unsent letter of a few lines to someone who helped you once.

title: One thing at a time
easy: Do one task for twenty-five minutes with every notification off.
medium: Spend a whole morning with your phone in another room.
brave: Turn the phone off from dinner until breakfast.
indoor: Watch or read one thing start to finish without checking anything else.
why: Doing one thing fully is rare now. That makes it worth practicing.
pen: Write what happened when you felt the urge to check. Then write what you told yourself about it.

title: Find something new on a known path
easy: On a route you know well, find three details you never noticed.
medium: Walk your usual route in the opposite direction and note what changes.
brave: Spend twenty minutes in a place you pass every day, and draw a map of it from memory afterwards.
indoor: Find five things in your home you have stopped seeing.
why: Habit makes us blind. Attention gives the world back.
pen: For two minutes, write sentences that begin with "Right now I notice..."

title: Use your body on purpose
easy: Take the stairs every time today.
medium: Walk or cycle somewhere you would normally drive or ride to.
brave: Go for a run or a long swim, at an honest pace.
indoor: Do ten slow squats, ten push-ups and a one-minute stretch.
why: Action comes before motivation. Move first, and the mood follows.
pen: Write three "I have to" sentences about your body. Rewrite each as "I choose to" or "I won't".

title: Write a real letter
easy: Write a postcard to someone and post it.
medium: Write a one-page letter by hand to someone you care about.
brave: Write a letter to someone you lost touch with, and send it.
indoor: Write a short note by hand and leave it where someone at home will find it.
why: A letter takes time to write, which is exactly why it matters.
pen: Write what you wanted to say in the letter but left out, and why you left it out.

title: Sit under a tree
easy: Find a tree and stand next to it for three minutes.
medium: Sit under a tree for fifteen minutes. Nothing to do.
brave: Spend an hour in a park or forest with no plan.
indoor: Water a plant and look at it closely for three minutes.
why: Trees grow slowly and do not hurry. You can borrow that.
pen: Make two columns: what is up to me this week, and what is not.

title: Share a meal
easy: Eat one meal today with someone, phones away.
medium: Invite someone for coffee or a walk this week, and set the date today.
brave: Cook for someone and eat together without any screens.
indoor: Call someone who lives far away and share a meal over the phone.
why: Shared meals are one of the oldest ways people stay close.
pen: Write what went well in the conversation, what didn't, and what you would do next time.

title: Make the phone boring
easy: Switch your phone to greyscale for the day.
medium: Move every social app off your home screen.
brave: Delete the one app you open most without thinking. You can install it again tomorrow if you choose.
indoor: Turn off every non-human notification.
why: Your phone is designed to pull at you. You can change the design.
pen: Write the facts about how you used your phone today. Then write your judgment about it. Keep them apart.

title: Collect three colours
easy: Find three things outside that are the same colour.
medium: Find ten shades of green on one walk.
brave: Spend half an hour noticing only shapes and colours, naming nothing.
indoor: Find every shade of one colour in your home.
why: Looking closely is a skill. Skills grow with practice.
pen: Describe one ordinary object you saw today in so much detail that a stranger could draw it.

title: Breathe slower than usual
easy: Take ten slow breaths: four in, six out.
medium: Sit still for five minutes and only breathe.
brave: Sit for fifteen minutes. When your mind wanders, bring it back without scolding it.
indoor: Lie on the floor for five minutes and breathe into your belly.
why: Your breath is one of the few things fully up to you.
pen: For two minutes, write sentences that begin with "Right now I notice..."

title: Fix one broken thing
easy: Fix something small: a loose button, a squeaky door, a messy drawer.
medium: Repair something you were going to throw away.
brave: Learn to fix something you always paid someone else to fix, and do it.
indoor: Tidy and repair one corner of your home.
why: Repair is patient work. It teaches care for what you already have.
pen: Write three "I have to" sentences about your home. Rewrite each as "I choose to" or "I won't".

title: Go somewhere new nearby
easy: Take a street you have never walked down.
medium: Visit a park, shop or library nearby that you have never entered.
brave: Take a train or bus to a place you have never been, and walk around for an hour.
indoor: Rearrange one room so it feels like a new place.
why: Small novelty wakes up attention without needing anything big.
pen: Describe today's new place as if you were seeing your whole town from a hill far away.

title: Call instead of text
easy: Answer one message today with a call instead.
medium: Call a friend you have not spoken to in a month.
brave: Call someone with whom things were left unfinished. Keep it simple.
indoor: Record a voice message for someone instead of typing.
why: A voice carries what text cannot.
pen: Write an unsent letter of a few lines to someone you miss.

title: Leave a moment empty
easy: The next time you wait in line, don't take out your phone.
medium: Ride or walk to wherever you go today with no headphones.
brave: Spend one hour alone with no phone, book or music.
indoor: Sit by a window for ten minutes with nothing in your hands.
why: Boredom is where your own thoughts get room to speak.
pen: Write what you thought about when there was nothing to fill the time.

title: Notice by touch
easy: Close your eyes and identify five things by touch alone.
medium: Walk barefoot on grass, sand or earth for five minutes.
brave: Spend a meal eating slowly with your eyes closed for the first five bites.
indoor: Hold a cup of something warm and notice it for two minutes.
why: Your body notices what your mind skips over.
pen: Write the facts of one moment today. Then write what you told yourself about it.

title: Move outdoors
easy: Stretch outside for five minutes.
medium: Do a twenty-minute brisk walk, faster than comfortable.
brave: Climb the highest point you can reach on foot nearby.
indoor: Dance to three songs with the door closed.
why: The body is not a vehicle for the head. Treat it like a companion.
pen: Write what went well in your body today, what didn't, and what you will try tomorrow.

title: Write one page
easy: Write five lines about a memory from childhood.
medium: Write one full page on any subject. Don't stop to correct.
brave: Write a short story, poem or essay and read it to someone.
indoor: Copy a passage you love by hand, slowly.
why: Writing by hand slows thinking down enough to see it.
pen: Write a few lines to your future self, one year from today. Don't send it anywhere.

title: Go out in any weather
easy: Step outside for five minutes, whatever the weather.
medium: Take a walk in weather you would normally avoid.
brave: Spend an hour outside in rain, wind or cold, dressed for it.
indoor: Open the window wide for ten minutes and feel the air.
why: The weather is not up to you. How you meet it is.
pen: Make two columns: what was up to me today, and what was not.

title: Help without being asked
easy: Do one small helpful thing for someone without mentioning it.
medium: Offer an hour of your time to someone who could use it.
brave: Help a stranger with something real: directions, a bag, a question.
indoor: Do one household task that is usually someone else's.
why: Acting for others is one of the surest ways out of your own head.
pen: Write what you did. Then write what you hoped it would mean. Keep them apart.

title: A day without feeds
easy: No social feeds until noon.
medium: No social feeds today.
brave: No social feeds for the next three days. Tell one person about it.
indoor: Replace your evening scroll with a book or a paper.
why: A feed never ends. Your day does. Choose what fills it.
pen: Write three "I have to check" sentences. Rewrite each as "I choose to" or "I won't".

title: Watch one living thing
easy: Watch a bird, insect or animal for two minutes.
medium: Watch the same tree or plant for ten minutes, noticing movement.
brave: Spend half an hour watching one place change: light, people, animals.
indoor: Watch a houseplant or the view from a window for ten minutes.
why: Patience is learned by watching things that do not hurry.
pen: Describe your life this week as if you were that small creature looking up at it.

title: Go to bed earlier
easy: Go to bed fifteen minutes earlier than usual.
medium: No screens in the last hour before sleep.
brave: Charge your phone outside your bedroom tonight.
indoor: Read on paper for twenty minutes before sleep.
why: Tomorrow's patience is decided partly by tonight's sleep.
pen: Write what went well today, what didn't, and what you will do differently tomorrow.

title: Give something you made
easy: Make a drawing or note and give it to someone.
medium: Bake or cook something and share it.
brave: Make a small gift by hand for someone, and give it in person.
indoor: Write a card by hand for someone you live with.
why: What you make carries your time in it. People feel that.
pen: Write an unsent letter of a few lines to the person you made it for.
